title: Dark Pattern Audit Episode (v2)
description: ADDITIVE extension of episode.v1.schema.json. Every v1 top-level field is reused here by pointer with its exact v1 name, type, and meaning unchanged (audit_metadata, website_context, journey_steps, temporal_checks, disclosure_context, and every nested $def they use). schema_version and eight new blocks (episode, steps, outcome, privacy, evidence, attributes, ccpa_verdict, mechanism_verdict) are added alongside them, never replacing them. See journey/schema_migration.py for the v1-to-v2 migration shim.

ccpa_verdict.description: Existing v1 judge output (prompts/pattern_prompt_judge.txt's {findings:[...]} shape), unchanged. Empty object until llm/judge.py is implemented and run.

mechanism_verdict.description: Filled later from manual LLM ingest, Phase 4. Empty object until then.

goal.description: A goal id from the goal library (config.yaml goals[].id), or null if this episode wasn't recorded against a specific goal (e.g. migrated v1 data never tracked one).

locale.description: Nullable: v1 never captured locale, so migrated episodes carry null here rather than a fabricated value.

collection_mode.description: Only 'manual' exists in Stage 1; the enum is expected to grow in a later, still-additive schema revision.

group_evidence_path.description: Path (relative to output.root, i.e. this episode's grandparent directory) to the group_evidence.json this episode was last included in, or null if extract-group-evidence has never run for its (site_id, goal) group. Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2. See journey/group_evidence_extractor.py.

redacted_headers.description: Lowercase NAMES (never values) of headers that were present and withheld -- e.g. ["authorization","cookie"] -- see recorder/masking/network_masker.py. Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2.

screenshot_path.description: Path to an UNMASKED screenshot in the episode folder. Always null once masking is active (see recorder/masking/): the unmasked image is never written to the episode folder, only kept transiently in a temp dir (privacy.keep_raw_artifacts). Non-null only for pre-masking-era data.

dom_snapshot_path.description: Path to an UNMASKED DOM snapshot. Always null once masking is active, for the same reason as screenshot_path -- see dom_snapshot_masked_path.

dom_snapshot_masked_path.description: The masked DOM snapshot actually persisted in the episode folder (recorder/masking/dom_masker.py). Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2, mirrors screenshot_path/screenshot_masked_path's split.

capture_error.description: Non-null when screenshot or DOM capture failed for this step (recorder/interactive_v2.py records the step anyway rather than dropping it). Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2, existing v2 producers/consumers that don't set it will fail validation until they do (see journey/schema_migration.py, which now always sets this to null for migrated v1 steps).

tab_id.description: Which browser tab/page produced this step ('main' for the initial tab, a generated id for each popup/new-tab attached mid-session). Added alongside capture_error, same reasoning.

computed_styles_path.description: Path to a JSON file of computed CSS + geometry for this step's interactive elements (recorder/evidence_probe.py) -- selector/tag/text/tab_index/bounding_box/color/background_color/font_size_px/is_below_fold per element. Feeds signals/visual_asymmetry.py. Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2.

goal_achieved.description: Nullable: episodes with no goal-completion assessment (e.g. migrated v1 data, which never tracked this) carry null rather than a fabricated true/false.

masker_version.description: Nullable: null means no masking stage ran over this episode (e.g. migrated v1 data, recorded before any masker existed).

Evidence.description: Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2. Every property is OPTIONAL (an empty object {} still validates, matching pre-extractor episodes) but, once present, must match its documented shape. Populated by journey/evidence_extractor.py -- pure measurement over the stored (masked) episode, no LLM, no subjective judgement. See signals/friction.py, visual_asymmetry.py, claims.py, price_drift.py, path_deviation.py, complexity.py, stated_vs_actual.py.

ui_regions.description: One entry per interactive element recorder/evidence_probe.py captured, tagged by signals/ui_regions.py BEFORE any attribute agent runs -- see attribute_agents/base.py's build_region_map, the only place downstream that reads this. Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2.

text.description: Only present for a DISCLOSURE-tagged element (signals/ui_regions.py's data-disclosure opt-in pass) -- interactive elements omit this, their text already reaches evidence via computed_styles/the code agent's own evidence_pointers. Optional (additive), not required, so older stored episodes without it still validate.

region.description: Must exactly match config.ui_regions.REGION_IDS -- kept as a duplicated enum (same pattern as AttributeResult.attribute duplicating attribute_agents.base.ATTRIBUTES) so schema validation doesn't need to import Python config at validate time.

form_fields_required.description: Max count of required form fields ([required] attribute) found in any single step's masked DOM across the episode -- see signals/friction.py docstring for why 'max over steps' rather than a sum.

friction_ratio.description: this episode's step count / paired episode's step count. Null unless episode.paired_episode_id is set AND that episode's episode.json was found on disk -- never guessed.

contrast_ratio.description: positive element's own WCAG text/background contrast ratio, divided by the negative element's own -- >1 means the accept/keep/yes option is visually more prominent than the reject/cancel/no option.

normalized_value.description: The extracted quantity/duration where one exists (e.g. 2 for "only 2 left", seconds-remaining for a countdown), else null.

StatedVsActualEntry.description: route_changed is additive (not required) so already-stored v2 episodes whose stated_vs_actual predates this field still load -- journey/evidence_extractor.py always populates it for anything freshly extracted; attribute_agents/deception.py treats it as False when absent (same as never having route-changed).

route_changed.description: True if this step's URL differs from the immediately preceding step's -- a second, independent way a genuinely client-side-only action (no backend, e.g. a mock demo's React-state-only cancel) can show up without network_fired. attribute_agents/deception.py only treats an action as suspicious when NEITHER this nor network_fired is true.

Attributes.description: Added after v2's initial release -- additive, same schema_version:2. No required properties ({} still validates, matching pre-Phase-3 episodes). Populated by journey/attribute_runner.py (the run-attributes CLI) -- see attribute_agents/base.py for the per-result contract and the hard rules every result satisfies before landing here.

results.description: A list, not a dict keyed by attribute, because more than one agent (e.g. a code agent now and an LLM agent later) may assess the same attribute -- each result is independently tagged with which attribute/agent produced it.

step_id.description: Null for evidence sourced from group-level signals (claim_persistence, paired_flow_comparison, etc.), which span more than one episode/step and have no single step_id.

ui_region.description: Stamped by attribute_agents/base.py's build_region_map/enrich_evidence_pointers from episode.evidence.ui_regions -- never authored by an agent, never invented by an LLM (journey/mechanism_verdict_ingest.py rejects a Stage-2 response whose ui_region doesn't match the extractor's own tag for that (step_id, selector)). "unclassified" is the honest default when no region matched or selector is null.

signal.description: Dot-path identifying which measurement this points at, e.g. "visual_asymmetry.contrast_ratio". An image-sourced signal (the model actually looked at the attached screenshot for this specific claim) is prefixed "screenshot_visual_inspection" -- see signals/visual_claims.py.

verdict.description: not_assessable is required (not 'no') when the necessary signal was null/missing -- see attribute_agents/base.py's required_signals mechanism, which enforces this in the framework rather than trusting each agent.

evidence_pointers.description: A verdict of fires/unsure with an empty list here is impossible in stored data -- attribute_agents/base.py downgrades any such result to 'no' before it can be written.

visual_claim_unverified.description: OPTIONAL 9th field, present only when relevant. A Stage-2 LLM verdict whose reasoning makes a visual claim (see signals/visual_claims.py) must set this true UNLESS at least one evidence_pointer's signal is image-sourced (prefixed "screenshot_visual_inspection") -- journey/mechanism_verdict_ingest.py enforces the OR at ingest time. Absent (not false) for every code-agent result and every LLM result with no visual claim at all -- code agents structurally can never have this be true, see attribute_agents/base.py's hard visual-claim guard.
